AbortReason.description: Why the host ended a run (`run_aborted`).

key.description:
The key, `ptc_sk_…`, to send as `Authorization: Bearer ptc_sk_…`. Only in the answer
to `POST /v1/api-keys`.

CallAttempts.description: How many times a tool call was sent.

Callsite.description: A position in the script's TypeScript source (`script.ts`), 1-based.

CancelReason.description: Why a run is being cancelled.

CancelRun.description:
`POST /v1/runs/{id}/cancel`: every pending await of the script rejects with
`CancelledError`; the script gets one activation to clean up.

oneOf.description: Wait up to this long for the run to end before answering.

CheckRequest.description:
`POST /v1/check`: type-checks a script against the sandbox lib and a toolset's
declarations, in strict mode, before anything runs.

script.description: The TypeScript source: a single ES module whose default export is the entry point.

toolset.description: The toolset whose `ptc:tools` the script imports. Without one, `ptc:tools` is empty.

CheckResult.description: The diagnostics of a check. A script with only warnings passes.

CompleteTask.description: `POST /v1/tasks/{token}/complete`: the tool's result, delivered to the script.

CreateApiKey.description:
`POST /v1/api-keys`: a key `ptc_sk_…` for a tenant. Keys are stored hashed: the key itself
is only in this answer.

allowedLabels.description:
The key only sees runs carrying all these labels: an agent's tools see only their own
conversation's runs.

name.description: What the key is for, for the operator.

events.description: The events to send. Every event when empty.

labels.description:
Only events about runs carrying these labels. A key limited to labels can only
subscribe within them.

url.description: An HTTPS URL of the harness.

CreateToolset.description:
`POST /v1/toolsets`: MCP servers, host tools and the `http` tool, with a policy per tool.
Registering connects to the MCP servers, lists their tools and pins their schemas. The
toolset is content-addressed: registering the same toolset twice gives the same id.

host.description: Ask the end user a question and return their answer.
host.name: ask_user

oneOf.description:
Credentials of the MCP servers: used to list their tools, and kept as the toolset's
credentials, as `PUT /v1/toolsets/{id}/credentials` sets them. They are not part of the
toolset's id.

host.description:
Host tools: functions of the harness, executed by its SDK worker (`GET /v1/tasks`). A
name `group.tool` puts the tool in the `group` namespace of `ptc:tools`.

oneOf.description: Enables the built-in `http` tool, and `fetch` in scripts, for these hosts only.

mcp.description: MCP servers. Their tools are called by ai-ptc and named `<server>.<tool>`.

Credentials.description:
`PUT /v1/toolsets/{id}/credentials` and `PUT /v1/runs/{id}/credentials`: secrets injected
into the MCP transport at call time. They never enter the journal, the isolate, a cassette
or OpenTelemetry; a call uses the run's credentials if it has some, else the toolset's.
Setting them replaces the previous ones, and makes ready again the calls parked by
`credentials.expired`.

CredentialsExpired.description:
A call parked because the server refused the credentials. Renew them with
`PUT /v1/runs/{id}/credentials` or `PUT /v1/toolsets/{id}/credentials`: the call is then
sent again with the same idempotency key.

dts.description: `ptc-tools.d.ts`: the `ptc:tools` module, with tool descriptions as JSDoc.

prompt.description: The compact rendering for the model's prompt, one line per tool.

DeferTask.description:
`POST /v1/tasks/{token}/defer`: the handler will answer later, possibly days later, with
`/complete` or `/fail` and the same token. No heartbeat is needed meanwhile.

oneOf.description:
Fail the call with `timeout` if no answer comes within this time. Bounded by the run's
TTL, which is the default.

Diagnostic.description:
One finding of the checks: tsgo's type errors, the checks at start, and the checker's own
rules. Written for a model.

example.message: Type 'number' is not assignable to type 'string'.

code.description:
`TS<n>` for tsgo; `ptc/<rule>` for the checks at start and the checker's own rules
(`ptc/floating-promise`, `ptc/ignored-async-callback`, `ptc/absent-global`…).

frame.description: A few lines of the source around the location, with the span underlined.

hint.description: What to do instead, when the checker knows (the hint of an absent global, for example).

oneOf.description: Where in `script.ts`; absent for a diagnostic about the script as a whole.

Duration.description: A duration: a number and a unit (ms, s, m, h, d, w), possibly several ("1h30m"), or a number of milliseconds.

oneOf.description: milliseconds

idx.description: Position in the history: from 0, contiguous.

recordedAt.description:
When the entry was committed; monotonic per run. Once a trigger is delivered, it is the
script's logical time.

Event.description: A journal event (`archi/02-journal.md`): lifecycle, commands, completions and annotations.

oneOf.description: The run's first entry. The seed is left out: it is only in the exported journal.
The host ended the run.
The script started waiting for a signal whose mailbox was empty.

timeout.description: The `seq` of the timer of its timeout.

Expectations.description: What must be true at the end of a scenario. Everything not given is not checked.

calls.description: How many times each tool was called.

oneOf.description: The run failed with an error of this name, whose message contains `message`.

output.description: The output contains these values (objects are compared key by key, recursively).

FailTask.description:
`POST /v1/tasks/{token}/fail`: the tool failed. The script gets a `ToolError`, unless the
failure is retryable and the tool's policy is `retry`: the call is then made again, with
backoff.

message.description: The message of the `ToolError`, written for the model.

retryable.description: A transient failure: call again later.

ForkParent.description: The run a fork was started from.

at.description: The entry from which the fork was forced live, if the request gave one.

ForkRun.description:
`POST /v1/runs/{id}/fork` (`retry_run`): a new run with a corrected script. While its
commands match the parent's, the parent's recorded results are reused and no tool is called
again; it continues live at the first difference, at `at`, or at the end of the parent's
history (`archi/03-execution.md`, "Forks"). Takes `Idempotency-Key` as `POST /v1/runs`.

at.description: Go live from this journal entry even if the commands still match.

check.description: Type-check the corrected script first. `true` by default.

input.description: The fork's input. The parent's when absent.

oneOf.description:
The fork's labels. Absent, the fork keeps its parent's labels, so that whoever sees the
parent (the agent tools of a conversation, a key limited to labels) sees the fork.
A new TTL, from the fork's start. 30 days by default.

HeartbeatAck.description: `POST /v1/tasks/{token}/heartbeat`: the worker is still working on the task.

heartbeatTimeoutMs.description: The claim now expires if no heartbeat comes within this many milliseconds.

HostTool.description: A function of the harness, called by scripts and executed by the harness's SDK worker.

description.description: Shown to the model in the declarations.

inputSchema.description: JSON Schema of the arguments. Arguments are validated against it before the call.

outputSchema.description: JSON Schema of the result, for the declarations. Results are not validated.

HttpTool.description:
The built-in `http` tool: requests leave from the dispatcher, never from the isolate, and
only toward these hosts (`archi/04-tools.md`, "The `http` tool and egress").

allow.description: Host names, such as `api.example.com`. `*.example.com` allows the subdomains.

Identity.description:
`GET /v1/whoami`: who the API key is. Over the embedded server's socket, which takes no
key: the tenant `local`, with the role `admin`.

allowedLabels.description: The key only sees runs carrying all these labels.

keyId.description: The key's id (`DELETE /v1/api-keys/{id}`); absent without a key.

Labels.description:
Run labels: a bounded string map set when a run starts (agent, conversation, end user…).
They filter runs and scope API keys and webhooks. The script never sees them.

Location.description: A span in `script.ts`, 1-based, the end exclusive.

LogLine.description: One line of the script's console.

McpServer.description:
An MCP server: exactly one of `url` (streamable HTTP) and `command` (stdio).

A server of a deployment refuses `command` unless its configuration allows it: a stdio
server is a process started by ai-ptc. The embedded server accepts it.

command.description: The program of a stdio server.

env.description: Environment of a stdio server that is not secret. Secrets go in credentials.

name.description: The namespace of its tools in `ptc:tools`: an identifier.

policies.description:
Policies of its tools, by tool name as the server defines it. Tools not listed get the
default policy.

url.description: The URL of a streamable HTTP server.

OnInterruption.description: After an interruption (the dispatcher or the worker died mid-call).

Payload.description:
A JSON value carried by a run (its input and output, tool arguments and results, signal
payloads), identified by the SHA-256 of its canonical JSON (RFC 8785).

bytes.description: Size of the canonical JSON, in bytes.

digest.description: SHA-256 of the canonical JSON, lowercase hex.

preview.description: The start of the canonical JSON, for display.

value.description:
The value itself. Left out when it is larger than the endpoint returns inline
(`PAYLOAD_VALUE_LIMIT`, 256 KiB): read it with `GET /v1/payloads/{digest}`.

Problem.description: An error answered by the API, as `application/problem+json` (RFC 9457).

example.detail: run 0193a5c4-7d2e-7c1a-9b1e-3f6a2d9c8e10 has ended (completed): a signal can only be sent to a run that is still active
example.title: The run has ended

detail.description: What went wrong in this request, and what to do instead. Written for a model.

diagnostics.description: With `invalid-script`: why the script was refused, with locations in `script.ts`.

instance.description: The path of the request, or of the resource the problem is about.

title.description: A short summary of the kind of problem, the same for every occurrence.

Quarantine.description: Why a run is quarantined (`archi/03-execution.md`, "Non-determinism and quarantine").

reason.description: The replay mismatch, or the last error.

RejectTask.description: `POST /v1/tasks/{id}/reject`: the call fails with a `ToolError` carrying this message.

message.description: Why, written for the model. "rejected by the harness" when absent.

Role.description: What a key may call. The key's tenant scopes everything it sees.

Run.description: The state of a run: a projection of its journal, with its metadata.

oneOf.description: With `aborted`: why the host ended the run.

attempts.description:
How many times each tool call was sent, by seq, for the calls sent more than once: a
call retried after a transient failure, or sent again after its worker or dispatcher
died. Attempts live in the tool tasks, not in the journal: the read model keeps them.

epoch.description: The determinism epoch the run started under.

oneOf.description: With `failed` or `cancelled`: how the script failed.

expiresAt.description: The deadline: the run is cancelled then (reason `ttl`).

oneOf.description:
The input of `main`. Absent while the run is `pending`: its `run_started` waits in its
inbox for the first activation, which commits it.

logs.description: The last log lines of the script (`console.*`), oldest first, at most 20.

oneOf.description: With `completed`: what `main` returned.
For a fork, the run it was forked from.

Set while the run is quarantined: its activations are stopped until it is released or
given up. Quarantine is not a status.

traceId.description:
The OpenTelemetry trace the run belongs to: the caller's if it gave a `traceparent`,
else derived from the run id. 32 hex digits.

waitingFor.description: With `active`: what the run waits for.

RunCounts.description: A number of runs per status.

RunError.description: How a script failed, with where, for a model to fix it.

oneOf.description: The tool call whose failure the script did not catch, if that is how it failed.

frame.description: A few lines of the source around `location`.

oneOf.description: The innermost frame of the stack in `script.ts`.

stack.description: Source-mapped to `script.ts`, without the runtime's frames.

RunEvent.description: The run an event is about, in the state the event left it in.

RunMode.description:
`live`: tools are really called and time is real. `mock`: tools are answered by cassettes
and mocks, and time is virtual.

nextCursor.description: Pass it as `cursor` to read the next page; absent on the last page.

RunStatus.description:
The status of a run, a function of its journal (`archi/02-journal.md`, "Run state").
Quarantine is not a status: see `Run.quarantine`.

RunSummary.description: A run in a list, from the read model.

error.description: With `failed` or `cancelled`: the error's name. With `aborted`: the abort's kind.

headline.description: The first line of the script that is not blank, for display.

ScenarioSignal.description: A signal sent during a scenario.

when.description:
When it is sent: `"blocked"` (the default) once the run can advance no further without
the outside world; or a duration of virtual time after the start, such as `"2h"`.

Script.description: `GET /v1/scripts/{digest}`: one script's source, and what its runs did.

firstRunAt.description: When its first and last runs started; absent when no run is kept.

headline.description: The first line of the source that is not blank, for display.

runs.description: Runs of this script, by status, as the read model keeps them.

ScriptError.description:
How a script failed: what `main` threw, the rejection it left unhandled, `DeadlockError`,
or `CancelledError`.

stack.description: The stack, source-mapped to `script.ts`, without the runtime's own frames.

nextCursor.description: Pass it as `cursor` to read the next page; absent on the last page.

ScriptSummary.description: A distinct script: content-addressed, so every run of the same source counts here.

digest.description: SHA-256 of the TypeScript source, lowercase hex.

headline.description: The first line of the source that is not blank, for display.

labels.description: The labels its runs carried, with the number of runs for each `key:value`.

runs.description: Runs of this script, by status.

env.description: Environment variables of a stdio server.

headers.description: HTTP headers sent to a streamable HTTP server, such as `Authorization`.

ServerInfo.description:
`GET /v1/server`: what this server is. Every response also carries the `Ptc-Version`
header.

embedded.description: `ptc server --embedded`: one tenant, `local`, on a unix socket without a key.

epochs.description: The determinism epochs this server's workers support. New runs start under the last.

version.description: The version of the `ptc` binary. A CLI of another version restarts an embedded server.

virtualTime.description: Time is virtual: timers fire as soon as nothing else can advance.

SignalAccepted.description: `POST /v1/runs/{id}/signals/{name}`: the signal was put in the run's mailbox.

duplicate.description: The `Idempotency-Key` was already used for this run: nothing was added.

StartRun.description:
`POST /v1/runs`: starts a run. The script is compiled, checked and type-checked first; a
script that cannot run is refused (`invalid-script`) before any run exists.

With the `Idempotency-Key` header, a request repeated with the same key returns the run the
first one started, instead of starting a second one.

check.description: Type-check the script before starting it. `true` by default.

oneOf.description: Credentials of this run, set before its first call (as `PUT /v1/runs/{id}/credentials`).

labels.description:
Run metadata: filters runs, scopes `list_runs`, API keys and webhooks. The script never
sees them.

script.description: The TypeScript source: a single ES module whose default export is the entry point.

toolset.description: The toolset the script imports from `ptc:tools`. Without one, `ptc:tools` is empty.

traceparent.description:
W3C trace context of the caller (typically the LLM call that wrote the script): the run
appears under it in the caller's trace.

oneOf.description:
The run's TTL: it is cancelled at its deadline. 30 days by default, up to the
deployment's maximum.

Wait up to this long for the run to end before answering. Without it, the answer comes
as soon as the run exists.

StreamEvent.description:
One event of the stream. On the wire, each is a server-sent event whose `event` field is
the `type` below, whose `data` is this JSON object, and, for an entry, whose `id` is the
entry's `idx`.

allOf.description: A committed journal entry. Payload values above 256 KiB are left out.

oneOf.description: A committed journal entry. Payload values above 256 KiB are left out.

The last event of a stream: the run has ended, or, without `follow`, every entry
committed so far was sent.

secret.description: The signing secret, `whsec_…`. Only in the answer to `POST /v1/subscriptions`: keep it.

Task.description:
A claimed host-tool call. The worker keeps the claim alive with heartbeats, and answers
with `/complete` or `/fail`, or `/defer` to answer later.

args.description: The arguments, validated against the tool's input schema.

attempt.description: From 1. Above 1, an earlier attempt was interrupted.

heartbeatTimeoutMs.description: The claim expires if no heartbeat comes within this many milliseconds.

id.description: The task's id, as listed in the run's state.

idempotencyKey.description:
`{run_id}/{seq}` (a fork's call made again keeps its parent's), the same on every
attempt: the handler uses it to recognize a call it already made.

timeoutMs.description:
The tool's execution timeout, in milliseconds: past it, the call is not waited for any
more. Absent when the tool has none, the default of host tools: the run's TTL bounds it.

token.description: The claim's secret token: `/v1/tasks/{token}/…`. It changes with each claim.

traceparent.description: W3C trace context, with the tool call's span as parent.

TaskBatch.description: The tasks claimed; empty when `wait` passed without one.

TaskState.description: The state of a tool task.

TestRequest.description:
`POST /v1/test`: runs a script in mock mode, in virtual time, against a cassette, mock
handlers and static responses, and checks expectations (`archi/05-testing-and-observability.md`,
"Testing and mocks"). It is what `ptc test scenario.json` runs, with the files inlined.

cassette.description:
A cassette of the stored format v1, recorded from a real run
(`GET /v1/runs/{id}/journal?as=cassette`). Tried first.

mocks.description: TypeScript mock handlers, run in a separate isolate. Tried after the cassette.

signals.description: Signals sent to the run, in order.

tools.description:
Static responses per tool, tried last: the result, or `{"$error": "message"}` for a
failure (as in `ptc.tools.json`).

toolset.description: The toolset the script imports from `ptc:tools`.

calls.description: How many times each tool was called.

failures.description: The expectations that do not hold, one sentence each, written for a model.

trace.description: The LLM trace of the run (as `GET /v1/runs/{id}/trace?format=llm`).

policy.description: The policy with its defaults filled in.

server.description: The MCP server, for an MCP tool.

ToolFailure.description: How a tool call failed, as the script sees it (a thrown `ToolError`).

dts.description: The tool's declaration in `ptc-tools.d.ts`, with the types it uses.

prompt.description: The tool's line of the prompt rendering.

ToolPolicy.description:
A tool's policy, pinned in the toolset (`archi/04-tools.md`, "Policies"). Every field is
optional: what is not given takes its default.

approval.description:
The call waits for the harness's approval (`POST /v1/tasks/{id}/approve`) before it is
sent. Off by default.

concurrency.description:
At most this many calls of the tool in flight per run. The run's own limit (16) still
applies.

oneOf.description: How long a host tool's worker may go without a heartbeat. 60 seconds by default.
What happens to a call interrupted mid-flight. `retry` by default.
How long one attempt may take. 5 minutes by default for MCP tools.

ToolSchemaChanged.description:
A call parked because the tool no longer matches its pinned schema
(`archi/04-tools.md`, "When a toolset changes during a run"). Approve the task to continue
against the new schema, reject it, fork the run, or cancel it. The pinned schema is in the
toolset; `message` says what changed.

message.description:
What changed, as the dispatcher saw it: the tool is gone, its input schema refuses the
call's arguments, or its output schema changed. Written for the harness developer and
the model.

toolset.description: The run's toolset, where the pinned schema is.

ToolSearchResults.description: The tools matching a search, best first.

errors.description: Calls that failed, whatever the kind.

latencyMs.description:
From `schedule_tool_call` to the completion, in milliseconds, over the calls that have an
outcome; zeros when none has.

retries.description: Attempts beyond the first, over every call.

id.description: The digest of the pinned toolset (SHA-256, lowercase hex). Runs record it.

tools.description: Every tool a script of this toolset can call, sorted by name.

ToolsetList.description: `GET /v1/toolsets`: the toolsets registered by the tenant, by id.

ToolsetSummary.description: A registered toolset, without its schemas and declarations.

tools.description: The names of its tools, sorted.

Waiting.description: Something an active run waits for.

oneOf.description: A tool call in flight, and the state of its task.

args.description: The call's arguments: what the harness approves or rejects.

oneOf.description: With `parked`: why.
A durable timer: `sleep`, `setTimeout`, `setInterval`, or a signal's timeout.
`await signal(name)` with an empty mailbox.

timeoutAt.description: When the wait gives up and returns `undefined`, if it has a timeout.

WebhookEvent.description:
The body of an outbound webhook: `{ "type", "timestamp", "data" }`, as Standard Webhooks
recommends. The delivery's id is the `webhook-id` header; a retried delivery keeps it.

oneOf.description: The run completed: `data.run.output` holds what `main` returned.
The script failed: `data.run.error` says how.
The run ended `cancelled`.
The host ended the run: `data.run.abort` says why.

An activation left the run waiting for something other than its tool calls in flight:
a signal, a timer, or a task that waits for the harness. `data.run.waitingFor` says
what.
The run was quarantined: `data.run.quarantine` says why. Release it or give it up.
A call was parked because the server's schema of the tool changed during the run.
A call was parked because the server refused the credentials (401).

apiKey.description: An API key of the tenant. The embedded server's unix socket takes none.

info.description: The HTTP API /v1 of ai-ptc: toolsets, scripts, runs, host-tool tasks, webhooks, reading and administration. Every request carries an API key as a Bearer token (`ptc_sk_…`), except over the embedded server's unix socket and to the inbound webhook URL. Errors are `application/problem+json`, with a `detail` written for a model. Fields are camelCase, enumerated values snake_case, times RFC 3339, and durations a number and a unit (`"30s"`, `"1h30m"`) or a number of milliseconds.

idempotency key.
